findings.claim: The loop-9 leak probe builds its marker exception with type.getConstructor(String.class) on the real failure's class and returns 'no leak' when that fails (lines 481-486). Class.getConstructor sees only public constructors, so when the booking service throws a NoSuchElementException subclass without a public (String) constructor, the probe is skipped and a handler that copies the exception message into its body passes. How a learner reaches it: the reading's example throws its own not-found exception built from the id (new InvoiceNotFound(id)); a learner who mirrors that with a subclass of NoSuchElementException taking the id (or the id and owner), which still satisfies 'throw a NoSuchElementException' in the BookingService TODO, and who then writes the detail from the exception's message against the ApiErrors TODO ('The detail must not repeat the exception message'), passes all 10 tests. Critic runs at 4e96e5c0140ee973b11b6b17752964b926f8f02c, JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16 offline, on the private solution with BookingService throwing such a subclass and ApiErrors setting the problem detail to the exception message: with only an (id, owner) constructor, and again with an added package-private (String) constructor, all 10 tests pass while the real 404 bodies for Grace's requests for booking 2 and 999 repeat the exception text ('No booking 2 for grace'); the control with a public (String) constructor fails the row with 'the error body still reveals the exception'. The real-body checks (type name, 'Exception', stack frame) cannot see learner-worded text, which is why the probe exists. Low: it needs two deviations from the handed TODOs, the leaked text here is the learner's own wording, and the #o3 choice itself is unaffected.

evidence.section: getConstructor(Class<?>...) ('reflects the specified public constructor of the class')
Exception Mapping and Method Arguments ('Exception type - For access to the raised exception')
Is the API Vulnerable? ('Error messages include stack traces, or expose other sensitive information')
Teaching (custom not-found exception built from the id)

findings.recommendation: Build the probe from the nearest type in the failure's class hierarchy that has a (String) constructor (use getDeclaredConstructor with setAccessible so package-private ones count), walking up to NoSuchElementException, and resolve that through the same handlerExceptionResolver; or, when no message constructor is found, fail closed only if the real body contains the failure's own non-blank message outside the required title. Add the subclass-with-echo variant to lab-run.json variantRuns.

Acceptance sweep at this head (scratch-only subclass of SecurityLabTest calling the five shipped row checks reflectively on the solved app after earlierTasks() returned null): 209 candidates (four callers times 40 method/path forms including case, query, fragment, trailing slash, doubled slash, dot-segment, percent-encoded, leading-zero, signed, overflow, template, both prerequisite probe paths, /error, /auth/register and /auth/token, plus 45 login forms with stolen, real, wrong, blank, null, 73-character and multi-byte passwords, plus 4 hand-built registration requests). No candidate passes two rows, neither probe path passes any row, and every accepted candidate is an instance of its own practice: a customer reaching the admin statistics endpoint (role checks); a login presenting the copied stored value for admin, grace or ada (hashing); a non-positive booking id with any caller's token (validation); a customer reading a booking of their own (DTO); a token-bearing request for a booking the caller does not own or that does not exist (safe error bodies). Practice-removal mutants with the solved rows unchanged each fail through their own row or prerequisite: raw password storage (hashing row names Task 1), @Positive removed (validation row names step 3), handler returning the entity (DTO row names steps 2 and 3), ApiErrors emptied (safe-errors row names step 4), chain method without @Bean (prerequisite names Task 2). So #o3 is practised by an executable learner act, checked behaviourally, and cannot be passed without making the practice-to-attack connection. Narrowed, not closed. What is fixed: register now takes a BindingResult and returns 400 itself, and the password carries @Size(max = 72). Critic embedded-server probe at 4e96e5c0140ee973b11b6b17752964b926f8f02c (scratch @SpringBootTest RANDOM_PORT test sending real HTTP with java.net.http, anonymous caller): blank username, missing password, blank password and a 73-character ASCII password each answer 400 and store nothing; a 72-character ASCII password answers 201. Still open: @Size counts characters (the Jakarta Validation spec, https://jakarta.ee/specifications/bean-validation/3.1/jakarta-validation-spec-3.1.html, @Size, retrieved 2026-11-19T06:39:45Z, sha256 ee0788edd40e360342dcdb66877739f886051b5776400b5ccece625758b78d43: 'CharSequence (length of character sequence is evaluated)'; JDK 25 String.length, https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html, retrieved 2026-11-19T06:39:38Z, sha256 d6fe54ea59fc2c32b57df32f03ec3af06d0c95043fb1c284d7d30a890b5729e2: 'the number of Unicode code units'), while bcrypt's limit is 72 bytes (OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html, 'Input Limits of bcrypt', retrieved 2026-11-19T06:38:52Z, sha256 9fdf8b41477e641594832cebd4dbb388d8d61ebe71c7d3a4bdec21d235fc8556: 'enforce a maximum password length of 72 bytes'). In the same probe a password of 40 accented letters (80 UTF-8 bytes), of 72 accented letters (144 bytes) and of 36 lock emoji (72 UTF-16 units, 144 bytes) each pass @Size, then Task 1's delegating bcrypt encoder throws IllegalArgumentException 'password cannot be more than 72 bytes' (in the surefire output), and the anonymous caller gets 401 with a Bearer WWW-Authenticate challenge and an empty body through the ERROR-dispatch mechanism this finding described; nothing is stored. The new comment (line 30, 'bcrypt reads at most 72 bytes, so a password over 72 characters is refused too') equates the two limits, and the method comment ('Answer a broken registration here with 400') is not true for these passwords. Side note, not part of this finding: malformed JSON, an empty body and a text/plain body also answer 401 for the same ERROR-dispatch reason; they are not validation errors, so BindingResult cannot see them. Low as before: no test, README step or step 6 row sends a registration. Recommendation: check the UTF-8 byte length (for example a small custom constraint, or a getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length check in the handler returning 400), and word the comment as a 72-byte limit; re-run the probe with a multi-byte password on the embedded server.
